Subject: DPA redlines: retention / backup carve-outs

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is LumenHealth's updated DPA redline. Our legal and security teams are comfortable with most of the language, but we have a few outstanding asks around data retention and backups for healthcare PII:

- We need a DR/backups carve-out so that backups can be retained beyond customer-deletion requests for a limited safe-harbor period (we proposed 180 days) strictly for restoration/DR.
- Any extended retention must include strict access controls, encryption, and audit logging; we flagged subprocessors used for backup storage and need confirmation.
- We also asked for a firm deletion confirmation timeline for primary copies (30 days) and transparency on tombstoning / crypto-erase procedures.

Can you confirm Redwood's ability to accept a limited backup carve-out and provide a short evidentiary packet (SOC2 + encryption notes + KMS usage)? We've attached the redline (Lumen_DPA_redline_v1.pdf).

Thanks — look forward to resolving quickly (we're aiming for DocuSign the week of 11/30).

Best,
Ellen Park
Senior Procurement Manager
LumenHealth

Team —

Reviewing Ellen's redline now. High-level thoughts:

1) Carve-out framing: we should accept a narrowly scoped "backup retention for restoration/DR" exception that is:
   - Timeboxable (we propose 90 days)
   - Limited to offline/immutable backup copies used solely for restoration
   - Subject to encryption (customer keys where available) and role-based access with logging

2) Deletion language: maintain primary deletion obligation (30 days) and require us to overwrite or tombstone primary copies; backup retention must not be used for other processing.

3) Subprocessors: we must enumerate the backup/replication subprocessors and include a clause requiring notice before engaging new ones. Recommend adding a subclause: "Redwood will provide a list of current backup subprocessors and provide 30 days' notice for changes; critical changes require advance security review."

I'll draft redline language and attach into RW-Response-DPA-v2.docx. Lauren, please confirm if finance needs a note on potential audit requests from Lumen. Rishi, can you provide the SOC2 excerpt + KMS notes.

- Karthik

Jasmine / Karthik —

Attached are the pieces Ellen requested. Summary below for email thread (short bullets we can paste into the response to Lumen):

- SOC2: Redwood Inference Type II report (summary extract attached). Control focus: backup integrity and access logging.
- Encryption: Primary + backup data encrypted at rest with AES-256; customer-managed keys supported via KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP KMS).
- Access controls: Backups stored in isolated buckets, access limited to a small ops SRE group; access is logged and reviewed monthly.
- DR retention: We maintain immutable backup snapshots; propose carve-out retention window = 90 days for restoration-only purposes.
- Subprocessors: Current backup/storage subprocessors: CloudStore Inc (us-east-1 replication), Snapshotify (replication orchestration). We will notify for any additions.

Link to DR playbook (internal): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cRW-DR-playbook

Happy to provide a SOC2 bridge or exec summary for procurement.

Rishi
